# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable and recent environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and required certificates
# - build-essential: Compiler toolchain (gcc, g++, make)
# - git: For cloning the application source code
# - ca-certificates: For secure network communications (e.g., git clone)
# - openmpi-bin & libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries
# Clean up apt cache to reduce image size
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes
# - Allow running as root, which is common in containers.
# - Force TCP communication over the primary network interface (eth0).
# - Disable InfiniBand/other high-speed interconnects not present in standard cloud VMs.
# - Allow oversubscription of CPU cores.
RUN echo "btl_tcp_if_include = eth0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = tcp,self,vader" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "orte_base_help_aggregate = 0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "rmaps_base_oversubscribe = 1" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set a working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Clone the latest branch of the AMG (Algebraic Multi-Grid) benchmark source code
# The canonical repository is LLNL/AMG. We'll clone it into a directory named 'amg2023'.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git amg2023

# FIX: Change directory to the root of the repository to build all dependencies first.
# The previous attempt failed because 'make' was run in the 'test' subdirectory,
# which does not build the required library dependencies.
WORKDIR /opt/build/amg2023

# Compile the AMG application. The root Makefile handles building all required
# libraries and then the final executable.
RUN make

# FIX: Copy the compiled executable from its actual output directory ('test/')
# to a system location on the PATH for easy access.
RUN cp test/amg /usr/local/bin/amg

# Clean up the build directory to remove source code and intermediate object files,
# reducing the final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/build

# Set the default working directory for the final image
WORKDIR /

kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg2023-test-run
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: amg -problem 2 -n 80 80 80 -P 4 4 3
    environment:
      OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: cma
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
  logging:
    quiet: true
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r7g.12xlarge
  size: 1
  tasks: 48

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# MiniCluster manifest to run the AMG benchmark on a single node.
# This configuration is for an AWS CPU instance environment managed by Kubernetes.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster job.
  name: amg2023-test-run
  # Deployment will be in the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster job. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks (processes) to run. This corresponds to flux -n <tasks>.
  tasks: 4
  
  # Strict logging mode to fail on any error.
  logging:
    strict: true
    
  # Do not automatically clean up the job pods upon completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false
  
  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The main command to execute. The Flux Operator will prepend `flux run -n <tasks> ...`
      # Running AMG with problem type 2 and a small problem size of 4x4x4 for testing.
      command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4
      
      # This is not a launcher pod; it's a worker pod that runs the application.
      launcher: false

updates.reason: Previous FOM (7.55e+03) is extremely low. Selecting a high-core-count instance (m7g.16xlarge) and significantly increasing the problem size to establish a meaningful performance baseline.

The previous FOM (1.59e+09) was very high, indicating the instance type is a good choice. Incrementally increasing the problem size in one dimension (from 64x64x64 to 96x64x64) to potentially further improve the FOM, as larger problems often scale better.

FOM decreased slightly with the last problem size increase (1.59e+09 -> 1.57e+09). Reverting to the previous best problem size and testing a different MPI process layout (-P 8 4 2) to optimize process communication.

FOM has peaked and is now decreasing on m7g.16xlarge. Switching to a memory-optimized instance (r7g.12xlarge) with more memory per core (8 GiB/core) to test if a larger problem size can achieve a higher FOM.

context.optimize:
Maximize the amg2023 figure of merit. You MUST maximize memory per CPU core. More cores are better.
The trick to optimizing this is THREADING. You MUST force OpenMP and any math libraries to use only one thread per MPI rank. On example is setting OMP_NUM_THREADS to "1". You might also consider setting OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism to "cma" as a conservative builder will set to none.
YOU MUST SLOWLY increase the problem size, one dimension at a time, by an increment no more than double the current to increase the FOM. A timeout may not require a smaller problem size but rather a different instance.
